messages:
Maya R: Heads up — getting pile of alerts from us-east-edge: multiple ALB target groups showing unhealthy targets and pods failing to register.
Maya R: Example from monitoring: 18/60 targets unhealthy, healthcheck TCP timeout 10s, backend status 502
Maya R: tcpdump from pod IP shows SYN from ALB node, SYN-ACK missing. Looks like return path being blocked :thinking:
Maya R: @Liam can you check recent network changes? I didn't touch loadbalancer/new infra rules.

Liam: saw the alerts, on it. I noticed a recent change pushed by secops at 12:05 to tighten NACLs on edge-subnets (ticket #SEC-421). Will inspect rules.

Liam: running quick check: ```
aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0a1b2c3d --query 'NetworkAcls[].Entries[] | [?RuleAction==`deny`]' --output table
# sample output:
# Rule 100: Deny | Inbound | Protocol: TCP | PortRange: 1024-65535 | CIDR: 10.1.0.0/16
# Rule 110: Allow | Inbound | TCP 80  | 0.0.0.0/0
``` 

Liam: NACLs are stateless — we added an inbound DENY for ephemeral port range from edge-subnet CIDR which drops return traffic from ALB ephemeral ports back to pod IPs. That would explain the SYN-ACKs getting dropped.

Diego: ohhh that matches tcpdump. ALB healthchecks originate from ALB nodes using ephemeral source ports. If inbound ephemeral is denied at the NACL level, backend never sees the response.

Maya R: so secops tightened NACL but forgot to allow ephemeral return traffic for ALB subnets. Can we patch quickly? What's the fastest rollback?

Liam: temporary mitigation: add an explicit inbound ALLOW rule for TCP 1024-65535 from the ALB subnets (we have the list in terraform) at higher priority than the deny. Or revert the DENY rule that landed in the last policy push.

infra-bot: deploy-plan created: revert-nacl-secops-SEC-421 (PR #4521). ETA ~15m if approved.

Diego: alternate short-term workaround: change the target group to instance mode (host targets) so ALB healthchecks come to node port and avoid pod IP return path, but that's noisy and requires drain/rotate.

Sonia: please do the NACL fix first — changing TG mode is disruptive for edge clusters. Also we need a postmortem and a change control item so secops doesn't push deny rules without checking ALB/target-group topology.

Liam: Agreed. I'm patching now to add ALLOW inbound TCP 1024-65535 from ALB subnets and then will push a revert PR for the DENY. Will notify when done.

Maya R: thanks. once patch is up I'll rerun healthcheck curl from a probe node: ```curl -v telnet://<pod-ip>:<port>``` and tcpdump to confirm SYN/SYN-ACK.

Liam: patch applied, ALLOW rule added, healthcounts are recovering — unhealthy down from 18 to 4 in 6 minutes. Rolling: :thumbsup:

Maya R: verifying: tcpdump now shows SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK completed. Pods re-registered. Monitoring looks green.

Sonia: filing follow-up: add gating in secops change runbook to check "edge ALB target groups" and a preflight test that verifies ephemeral port pairs are allowed when moving NACLs. I'll attach to SEC-421.

Diego: also adding a quick Nagios/Prometheus alert for spikes in ALB target unhealthy_count when NACL changes are committed.

Maya R: closing the incident thread for now. Thanks everyone. Will add notes to the infra-change log. :white_check_mark:
